blocks.text: Exact metrics on the base-14 path

This document is rendered with no --font flag: its text is set in Helvetica, one of the fourteen fonts every PDF viewer supplies, and nothing is embedded. pdfnative measures such text with a compact width table by default. metrics: "exact" switches to the Adobe Core 14 widths, glyph by glyph, so a justified line ends exactly where the viewer's Helvetica ends it.

The option is inert as soon as a registered font measures the text (--font latin --lang latin): an embedded font always brings its own advance widths. That is why this sample has a category of its own, rendered without the font flags the typography samples need.

Wide and narrow glyphs — WWWW MMMM against iiii llll — typographic punctuation such as “double” and ‘single’ quotes, the ellipsis… and the en dash – are the characters whose widths differ most. Over a justified paragraph the differences add up to different line breaks: compare this file with a render of the same document without the metrics key.

Illicit millilitre fillings will jiggle little: fifty-five WWF members hummed “MMM…” while William’s minimum – a million Wm² – became illegible.
